text:
Mike Evans departed the 49ers’ game against the Washington Commanders Monday night before halftime with an Achilles injury, further depleting a wide receiver corps that was already thin.

Coach Kyle Shanahan said Evans’ injury is the same soreness he had dealt with throughout the week, and the 49ers don’t believe he will be out long-term.

The free-agent signee was seen stretching his lower legs shortly before his final catch of the half. On that play, Evans looped behind Washington linebacker Sonny Styles after lining up in the slot and caught a low pass from Purdy, going to the ground.

He stayed down a few seconds, then got up with a hand from Commanders defenders and walked to the 49ers’ locker room with a team trainer. He was ruled out for the game just after halftime.

“It’s bothered him throughout the week. With his Achilles tendinitis, it flared up tonight,” Shanahan said. “Hope he recovers through the week and I don’t think it’s a long-term thing. It cost him this game for two quarters and hopefully he can play next week; if not, the rest of the group has to step up.”

Evans was questionable to play Monday with Achilles tightness and rib issues. He has played through rib pain the last several weeks after fracturing several ribs.

Already missing were Ricky Pearsall (season-ending knee surgery), Demarcus Robinson (ankle), Deebo Samuel (hamstring) and Christian Kirk (calf).

The six-time Pro Bowl receiver had three catches for 94 yards in the first half before leaving the game, including a 54-yard catch-and-run.

Evans, 33, was a key to the 49ers’ win last week in Seattle, connecting with Brock Purdy for 75 yards on a single fourth-quarter drive to help swing the game. He was clearly playing through pain in that game, and continued to look ginger Monday at Levi’s Stadium.

Evans came to the 49ers from the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the offseason on a three-year, $42.4 million contract. He entered Monday’s game with 24 catches for 326 yards and three touchdowns.

Washington also lost its top receiver in the game as Terry McLaurin went down clutching his knee late in the first quarter running a route along the left sideline. He was carted off the field to the Commanders’ locker room.

“It was just the same thing that was bothering him all week,” Shanahan said. “It acted up too much during the game and he couldn’t go. We’ll see how he feels this week.”

When asked if it was a “close call” whether to allow Evans to play with his injury, Shanahan said Evans’ inability to finish the game didn’t come as a surprise.

“It was a pretty close call in terms of he wasn’t able to (practice) all week,” Shanahan said. “It’s something he’s dealt with in the past in his career. He felt confident he’d be good today. So that was the confidence he gave me. But we knew he might not be able to last.”

Evans was playing his third straight game with two broken ribs, but he appeared on the injury report last week with his new Achilles injury. Before he exited Monday, Evans continued his stellar debut season with the 49ers.

The six-time Pro Bowl selection had three catches for 94 yards, including a 54-yard catch-and-run to set up the 49ers’ second touchdown that provided a 13-3 lead in the first quarter. Evans has 27 catches for 420 yards and three touchdowns in six games this season.

Without Evans, the 49ers finished with four available wide receivers: Jordan Watkins, Jacob Cowing, Brandin Cooks and Malik Turner, who was elevated from the practice squad Monday. Deebo Samuel (hamstring) is expected to miss multiple games after he was injured in a win against the Seahawks on Oct. 11. Demarcus Robinson (ankle) and De’Zhaun Stribling (ankle) are on injured reserve.

Special teams troubles: Following Christian McCaffrey’s first-quarter touchdown run, Eddy Piñeiro missed the extra point. It continued an odd trend for the 49ers' kicker, who has missed seven extra points across the past two seasons but has missed just four field goals.

Shanahan was blunt when asked about his level of concern with Piñeiro.

“Yeah. I mean, he’s got to make them,” Shanahan said. “He missed another one today and fortunately it didn’t get us, but I think everyone knows the answer to that. You’ve got to make your extra points.”

Piñeiro has missed three field-goal attempts this season. He missed just one in 2025, which helped him earn a four-year, $17 million contract extension during the offseason.

Another special teamer drawing unwanted attention: punt returner Jacob Cowing. The 25-year-old let a punt in the first quarter slip right through his hands. He recovered the ball, but the 49ers were forced to start that drive on their 4-yard line.

“Jake made a real bad decision on (that) one,” Shanahan said, added Cowing “had to let it go” into the end zone. “I don’t think he made a mistake on any of the others, but yeah, that was a bad decision by him.”

Shanahan’s words offered a shift in tone from a week ago, when Cowing also muffed a punt against the Seahawks and he said: “No, it wasn’t enough (to bench him). It’s something that he can’t do … but no, we’re not changing his position yet.”

Other injuries: Linebacker Luke Gifford (groin) and nickelback Upton Stout (shoulder) exited Monday night’s game and did not return.

Gifford filled in against the Commanders for Garret Wallow, who was out with a hamstring injury, and exited in the first half. Wallow, a rotational linebacker behind Fred Warner and Dre Greenlaw, will likely be out through the 49ers’ bye week, which comes after their next game in Atlanta. Greenlaw missed Monday’s game due to a suspension; rookie Jaden Dugger played in Greenlaw’s place.

Stout has been recovering from an AC joint sprain that he suffered Week 4 against the Broncos. He played the previous two games but has been limited during the week. Stout aggravated the injury Monday night. In his place, the 49ers put reserve safety Ashtyn Davis in the slot. Davis picked up an illegal contact penalty in the fourth quarter.

text:
The Washington Commanders lost star wide receiver Terry McLaurin early Monday night after he went down with what appears to be a significant knee injury.

McLaurin was running a route near the end of the first quarter of Washington's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers when he suddenly fell near the sideline at Levi's Stadium. Replay showed that McLaurin's left knee gave out on him and buckled as he was planting to the outside.

He remained down on the field for quite some time in front of the Commanders' bench, clearly in a lot of pain.

A cart eventually came out for McLaurin, and he hopped up and onto the vehicle under his own power with his entire left leg in a full air cast. Players from both teams then saw him off.

The Commanders quickly ruled him out with a knee injury. Head coach Dan Quinn said after the contest that they didn't have any details, but they were concerned that the injury was significant.

McLaurin had one catch for 27 yards in the contest before he went down.

McLaurin entered Monday with 203 receiving yards and a single touchdown in four games this season, his eighth in the league with the Commanders. He missed the team's loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London due to a hamstring injury he suffered at practice before that contest before returning the following week.

While it's unclear how long McLaurin may be sidelined, the injury is a tough sign for a Commanders group that is struggling this season. The Commanders sit at just 1-4-1, which has them in last in the NFC East race. While they rallied a bit late and had a good look at the win down the stretch on Monday night, they couldn't quite pull it off.

The win pushed the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 on the year, which is the best record in the league. Only two other teams, the Kansas City Chiefs and Minnesota Vikings, are also still undefeated.

The NFC East is still wide open, so the Commanders aren't completely out of the playoff hunt yet despite their rough start. But losing a target like McLaurin for a substantial amount of time is going to make things much more difficult for quarterback Jayden Daniels as they approach the midway point of the season.

Jalen Hurts' season is likely over.

The Philadelphia Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, released a statement on Monday, relaying that doctors discovered multiple blood clots in his lungs.

Hurts is now expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season as he undergoes treatment, NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported on Monday.

Hurts' recovery is expected to take three months, Rapoport and Schefter added, putting his return this season in doubt.

“Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition,” the Eagles and Lynn said in a statement.

“Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. 'blood thinners'). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.

“Jalen’s prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.

“We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery.”

The Eagles initially ruled out Hurts on Oct. 15 for Philadelphia's Week 6 game against the Panthers, and then placed the QB on injured reserve on Saturday.

In their original statement last week, the Eagles announced that Hurts first reported issues with his calf on Oct. 8 after he was cleated during Philadelphia's Week 4 loss to the Rams on Oct. 4. Hurts received treatment and was added to the Eagles' injury report on Oct. 9 as a full practice participant ahead of their trip to London for last Sunday's game against the Jaguars.

A "superficial blood clot" was revealed during an evaluation on Oct. 10 in London, but the Eagles said that medical staff and doctors determined that "Jalen could safely play" against Jacksonville.

A subsequent follow-up exam on Wednesday "revealed movement in the small blood clot," which led to him being ruled out for their game against Carolina.

Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni was asked on Monday if there was something he felt the team could have done differently regarding Hurts' status.

“I’m not a medical expert," Sirianni said. "I lean on our guys in all those situations. I’m a football coach. I lean on our medical experts in every single situation. I have full trust and full faith in them. It’s not just me that has major care for our players. It’s them as well. We are all there, and I’m glad to be part of an organization that cares about the guys the way our guys do.”

The Eagles currently sit at 2-4 but are in second place in the NFC East. Backup Tanner McKee started the Week 6 loss to the Panthers. The 26-year-old struggled to move the offense until the end of the double-digit defeat.

text:
The Washington Commanders lost star wide receiver Terry McLaurin early Monday night after he went down with what appears to be a significant knee injury.

McLaurin was running a route near the end of the first quarter of Washington's 23-17 loss to the San Francisco 49ers when he suddenly fell near the sideline at Levi's Stadium. Replay showed that McLaurin's left knee gave out on him and buckled as he was planting to the outside.

He remained down on the field for quite some time in front of the Commanders' bench, clearly in a lot of pain.

A cart eventually came out for McLaurin, and he hopped up and onto the vehicle under his own power with his entire left leg in a full air cast. Players from both teams then saw him off.

The Commanders quickly ruled him out with a knee injury. Head coach Dan Quinn said after the contest that they didn't have any details, but they were concerned that the injury was significant.

McLaurin had one catch for 27 yards in the contest before he went down.

McLaurin entered Monday with 203 receiving yards and a single touchdown in four games this season, his eighth in the league with the Commanders. He missed the team's loss to the Indianapolis Colts in London due to a hamstring injury he suffered at practice before that contest before returning the following week.

While it's unclear how long McLaurin may be sidelined, the injury is a tough sign for a Commanders group that is struggling this season. The Commanders sit at just 1-4-1, which has them in last in the NFC East race. While they rallied a bit late and had a good look at the win down the stretch on Monday night, they couldn't quite pull it off.

The win pushed the 49ers to a perfect 6-0 on the year, which is the best record in the league. Only two other teams, the Kansas City Chiefs and Minnesota Vikings, are also still undefeated.

The NFC East is still wide open, so the Commanders aren't completely out of the playoff hunt yet despite their rough start. But losing a target like McLaurin for a substantial amount of time is going to make things much more difficult for quarterback Jayden Daniels as they approach the midway point of the season.

SANTA CLARA, Calif. -- After playing through Achilles soreness for most of the first half of Monday night's game against the Washington Commanders, San Francisco 49ers receiver Mike Evans departed just before halftime because of an Achilles injury.

The 49ers initially labeled Evans as questionable to return but ruled him out early in the third quarter. They went on to win, 23-17.

"Same thing that was bothering him all week," coach Kyle Shanahan said after the game. "Acted up too much in the game and couldn't go. We'll see how he feels this week."

Shanahan added that he doesn't believe Evans will need additional testing on the Achilles.

With 1:10 left in the second quarter, Evans caught a 16-yard in-breaker from quarterback Brock Purdy. After Commanders safety Jeremy Reaves touched him down, Evans stayed on the field and stretched his right leg.

Niners medical personnel ran on the field, helped Evans up and then supported him as he slowly walked back to the locker room.

Evans did not practice all week because of an ongoing recovery from broken ribs and a sore Achilles. He had a questionable tag entering the game, with Shanahan saying after the game that it was a close call on whether he'd play.

"We knew he might not be able to last," the coach said.

Evans had three catches for 94 yards before exiting.

Without Evans, the only healthy Niners receivers available were Jordan Watkins, Brandin Cooks, Jacob Cowing and Malik Turner.

"Obviously having him out there, he's a Hall of Famer," Purdy told ESPN after the game.

"But I thought our guys stepped. We still got to find a way to make plays."

Sooner rookies log strong showings

Rookie defensive end R Mason Thomas didn’t light up the stat sheet on Sunday, but he played a key role in the Kansas City Chiefs’ win over the Los Angeles Chargers.

Thomas hit Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert in the red zone, forcing him to throw an incompletion. Thomas’ hit nearly forced Herbert to fumble, but the veteran signal caller was able to throw the ball forward and avoid the turnover.

The former Oklahoma edge rusher appeared on 33 snaps and logged a 63.9 Pro Football Focus (PFF) defensive grade.

Thomas was a star throughout his four seasons in Norman. He ended his college career with 65 tackles, 25.5 tackles for loss, 17 sacks, four forced fumbles, three fumble recoveries and a scoop-and-score touchdown.

The Chiefs selected Thomas with the No. 40 overall pick (second round) in the 2026 NFL Draft. Thomas has played on 178 snaps so far in his rookie season.

Wide receiver Deion Burks had his best game as a professional on Sunday.

Burks, a former Sooner playing with the Indianapolis Colts, logged a 36-yard reception in his game against the Tennessee Titans. He finished the 26-20 loss with two catches for 41 yards, and he also rushed once for seven yards.

The Colts picked Burks in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft. Burks spent his final two college seasons in Norman after transferring from Purdue.

Williams shines in first game back

Baker Mayfield and Jalen Hurts are both injured, and Kyler Murray and the Minnesota Vikings had the week off.

That made Caleb Williams, who spent only one season at OU, the only Sooner quarterback in action on Sunday.

Williams led the Bears to their eight-point win over the Falcons. He completed 30 of his 36 pass attempts for 305 yards and a touchdown.

Williams had missed the Bears’ last three games with a leg injury before returning on Saturday. He led Chicago to the playoffs in 2025.

Before becoming an NFL star, Williams began his college days at OU, where he became the Sooners’ starting quarterback midway through the 2021 season. Williams, though, followed coach Lincoln Riley to USC after only one year in Norman.

text:
At just 28 years old, and only 20 months removed from being named the Super Bowl MVP, Jalen Hurts is now on blood thinners to stave off what – without them – could be life-threatening blood clots in his lungs.

The Associated Press and others are reporting that the Philadelphia Eagles quarterback won’t play again this season, which would appear an obvious outcome since treatment for Hurts’ injuries – bilateral pulmonary emboli and deep vein thrombosis in medical jargon – requires three months on the blood thinners.

That much everyone can agree on. It is everything in between that makes the situation less cut-and-dry.

The Eagles, in conjunction with Hurts’ agent Nicole Lynn, have released two statements in the past four days detailing Hurts’ injury and treatment, citing the “interest of transparency.”

The timeline breaks down like this:

Left unanswered are two critical issues.

For starters, why was Hurts permitted to fly across the Atlantic twice? Along with injury, as in Hurts’ case, deep vein thrombosis can be caused by extended periods sitting on long flights, pulmonary critical care expert Dr. Parth Rali told CNN. The International Air Transport Association guidelines stipulate that “travelers with a recent DVT of the legs may fly once they are asymptomatic and stable on anticoagulants.”

A bigger question, though, is why was Hurts permitted to play in the game at all?

At best, he was coming off a handful of hours of rest after a stressful night in the hospital. At worst, he was competing with a serious medical condition.

During his normally scheduled Monday news conference, Eagles head coach Nick Sirianni did not go into detail about either decision, only repeatedly saying that he trusted his medical team and that “it’s not just me that cares deeply about our players, it’s them as well.”

Sirianni added that this was the same medical team that “helped 21 of 22 guys be available for the Super Bowl.” Asked how Hurts was feeling, the coach said he would keep his private conversations private.

“But I haven’t been without him for an extended period of time,” Sirianni said. “I miss him.”

As Sirianni spoke on a live-streamed interview, the chat box down the right side of the video erupted with unanswered questions. Even before the announcement about Hurts, Sirianni and the Eagles were on a short leash with their notoriously hard-to-please fan base. Philadelphia has lost four games in a row, the team’s worst skid in Sirianni’s six seasons.

Along with the usual “fire Sirianni” suggestions, fans directed their ire at Eagles owner Jeffrey Lurie and general manager Howie Roseman, who did not make themselves available for comment. Some called them cowards; others opted for more colorful language.

Most, however, questioned whether Hurts’ safety had been sacrificed in the name of the sport.

“Super Bowl MVP has been done wrong,” one wrote.

Added another, “Players’ health is at the forefront of our mind? Obviously not.”

Still another simply called the decision “shameful” and wondered who “put his life at risk.”

Deep vein thromboses, while rare, are not entirely uncommon among athletes. In February 2020, San Antonio Spurs star Victor Wembanyama was diagnosed with one in his shoulder, undergoing immediate surgery to prevent it from spreading to his lungs.

Week 6 wraps up in Santa Clara, where the Washington Commanders will visit the San Francisco 49ers for a "Monday Night Football" showdown. As Washington tries to inch closer to .500 on the season and rid itself of the sour taste of a tie with the Giants last week, it will have one of its key weapons on offense.

The status of Stefon Diggs was up in the air for this primetime matchup as the wideout dealt with a hamstring injury, but he is active. Diggs did not practice at the start of the week on Thursday, but returned to practice in a limited capacity on Friday and Saturday. Officially, he was listed as questionable.

Diggs, who signed a one-year deal with the franchise in early August, did not play in last week's tie with New York because of that hamstring.

49ers vs. Commanders prediction: Can San Francisco remain unbeaten? Full 'Monday Night Football' breakdown

Jared Dubin

When healthy, the 32-year-old has been a heavily involved figure within the Commanders offense, averaging just under eight targets per game so far this season. Because Terry McLaurin has also been in and out of the lineup due to injury, Diggs actually leads the team in targets (31), receptions (18), and receiving touchdowns (3). His 170 receiving yards are second to McLaurin (203).

What's fascinating about Diggs' tenure so far in Washington is that he's seen minimal time playing with quarterback Jayden Daniels. Because of injuries, there's only been one full game played between the two. That came in the season-opening loss to Philadelphia, where Diggs caught four of nine targets for 55 yards and a touchdown. Before Daniels left Week 2's loss to the Cowboys with a left elbow injury, the two connected for another touchdown. If/when these two can stay healthy and be on the field at the same time, they've flashed some explosiveness.

That'll be extremely important in this NFC matchup as the 49ers defense has been one of the stoutest in the league entering Week 6. San Francisco has the lowest explosive play rate allowed through five games by any team since 2000. Having a healthy Diggs would go a long way in putting a dent into that historic figure.

HOUSTON -- Texans wide receiver Tank Dell will return to the field against the New York Giants on Sunday after a 22-month hiatus, coach DeMeco Ryans announced Monday.

It will be the first game for Dell since the 2023 third-round pick missed all of the 2025 season after he suffered multiple torn ligaments and a dislocated kneecap in the Texans' Week 16 loss to the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024.

"No huge expectations from what he needs to do," Ryans said. "I'm just going to be excited to see him just out there for the first time in over two years, just getting some game action. So, I'm just thankful and grateful for him to have this opportunity to return. I don't have any expectations. I'm just happy to see him out there, and that's the only thing that matters."

Dell started the 2026 season on injured reserve when Houston made its 53-man roster cuts. He wasn't on the physically unable to perform list to start training camp but throughout camp he took part only in individual drills.

But Dell wasn't close to returning to game action during camp because there were only two days when he participated in team drills and only one was in pads -- on Aug. 10. But two weeks ago, his practice window opened and he has practiced with no setbacks.

text:
Injuries are piling up on top of losses for the 2-4 Los Angeles Rams.

Wide receiver Davante Adams suffered a hamstring injury in L.A.'s 18-16 loss to the Arizona Cardinals on Sunday and is expected to miss six to 10 weeks, head coach Sean McVay told reporters Monday.

NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport reported Adams is expected to have a procedure on his hamstring tendon to clean it out and the hope is he can return around the team's bye week or a little after. The Rams' bye falls on Week 11.

Adams, 33, was having another standout season for the Rams, with 30 receptions for 480 yards and four touchdowns while sporting a 16.0 yards-per-reception average, which would be the best in his career.

McVay announced a litany of injuries for the Rams in addition to Adams'.

Defensive tackle Poona Ford will miss the rest of the season with a ruptured triceps muscle, as will recent addition, kicker Blake Grupe, due to a knee injury. DT Kobie Turner (groin) is headed to injured reserve, guaranteeing he'll miss a minimum of four weeks.

Myles Garrett, who has been on IR since having knee surgery after the team's Week 1 loss in Australia, also won't start practicing this week.

"The first thing is you feel terrible for these guys," McVay said. "Those guys are key contributors for us, so there's a lot of emotions. But the first thing is support these guys, be there for them, and then the next thing is make sure that we figure out what's the best way for our team to be able to move forward in the absence of some critical factors for us."

Through six weeks, Adams was the Rams' receiving yards leader and the only pass catcher with multiple TD receptions. Puka Nacua, the team leader with 37 receptions who missed two games earlier this year, will continue to play a major role in the operation, as will tight ends such as Tyler Higbee and Colby Parkinson. Terrance Ferguson could factor in eventually, as well, though he's not eligible to come off IR until Week 8. Wide receiver Konata Mumpfield flashed in one of the games Nacua missed, going for 93 yards and a score on four catches, and there's also Jordan Whittington and Tutu Atwell.

With Ford and Turner going down, plus Garrett not on the way back yet, the Rams have some work to do to fortify their front seven. Aaron Donald and Braden Fiske will be tasked with some heavy lifting alongside larger roles for Tyler Davis and Larrell Murchison, the latter of whom has made only one appearance this season.

A laundry list of new injuries is not what the Rams needed as they find themselves at the bottom of the NFC West on Monday following a stunning loss to Arizona.

Behind the 2-4 Cardinals due to tiebreakers and staring up at the 3-3 Seahawks and unbeaten 49ers, the Rams have a long way to go to threaten for a division title -- and fewer pieces to help make it happen.

"We've taken some shots this year, and we've got to be able to get up and keep swinging," McVay said. "This is a good test."

The Los Angeles Rams are dealing more losses a day after they were upset by the Arizona Cardinals.

Wide receiver Davante Adams is out six-to-10 weeks with a ruptured hamstring and kicker Blake Grupe will miss the rest of the season after tearing his ACL in Sunday's loss, head coach Sean McVay told reporters on Monday.

Adams left Sunday's game with an apparent non-contact injury in the final minute and didn't return. Adams appeared to be holding his leg and hobbled off to the sideline where he was immediately seen by the Rams training staff.

Adams finished the game with three catches for 39 yards. He's eighth in the league in receiving yards (480) to go with 30 receptions and four receiving touchdowns this season, proving to still be a key pass-catcher for Matthew Stafford.

The injury marks another health setback for Adams after an injury cut his regular season short last year. He left a Week 15 win over the Detroit Lions in 2025 with a non-contact hamstring injury and missed the final three games of the regular season before returning for the playoffs.

Adams' best outing came in Week 2, when he had eight catches for 195 yards and two touchdowns in a 28-6 win over the Giants. He also scored twice in last Monday’s 37-34 overtime loss to the Bills.

As for the Grupe injury, he signed with the Rams last week after the team cut kicker Harrison Mevis amid his struggles. Grupe suffered his injury when he tried to make a tackle on a kick return. That put the Rams in a tricky spot for the remainder of Sunday's game.

With Sunday's loss, the Rams dropped to 2-4 on the season. They take on the Las Vegas Raiders in Week 7.

text:
Tank Dell is back.

The Houston Texans wide receiver will take the field on Sunday for their matchup with the New York Giants, head coach DeMeco Ryans confirmed on Monday. It will mark Dell's first game back since he went down with a gruesome knee injury in 2024.

"I don't have any expectations, I'm just happy to see him out there," Ryans said, via ESPN Radio's Will Kunkel.

"He is as quick as ever."

Dell caught a deep pass from quarterback C.J. Stroud in a matchup with the Kansas City Chiefs in December 2024. But as Dell was bringing the ball in, teammate Jared Wayne dove for the ball too and accidentally crashed into Dell's left knee. Dell made the catch, and completed the 30-yard touchdown, but the injury was gruesome.

He had to be driven off the field on a stretcher in what was a very emotional scene at Arrowhead Stadium. He remained in a Kansas City-area hospital overnight, and returned to Houston the next day.

Dell ended up tearing multiple ligaments, sustained meniscus damage and dislocated his left knee in the incident. It knocked him out of the entire 2025 campaign, and he's been recovering ever since.

The injury was just the latest significant one that Dell has already faced in his career. His rookie season was cut short after he fractured his fibula just 11 games in, and he was then shot in the leg as a bystander at a mass shooting in Florida in 2024. Dell recovered from both injuries in time to start the 2024 campaign normally.

Dell had 667 receiving yards and three touchdowns in 14 games during the 2024 campaign. The Texans selected him in the third round of the 2023 NFL Draft out of Houston.

Dell will rejoin the Texans at a critical time for the organization this season, too. After losing four straight to start the year, they've now won back-to-back contests entering Sunday's matchup with the Giants at NRG Stadium. They most recently rallied to beat the Jacksonville Jaguars in London on Sunday.

Though it's unclear if Dell will be able to compete at the same level he was at previously, considering how significant his knee injury and rehab actually was, he's finally ready to get back out onto the field. The next part of his playing career is here.

Fortunately, he was able to keep DeVonta Smith and Dallas Goedert afloat for fantasy managers, but the upside is clearly lacking. Saquon Barkley's eventual return will help and the Eagles have a pretty soft schedule until later in the year. Still, it's going to be tough to trust this unit for fantasy moving forward.

Mayfield: Tampa Bay may be getting its starter back in the fold soon. Reports over the weekend suggest Mayfield could be back in Week 7 against the Panthers. Mayfield pushed to play this past week in the loss to Pittsburgh, but Jalon Daniels got another start, finishing with 164 yards, 1 TD, 2 INTs and 39 rushing yards. text:
Jalen Hurts is expected to miss the remainder of the 2026 season, according to multiple reports, after blood clots were found in his lungs.

The Eagles and Hurts' agent, Nicole Lynn, issued a joint statement on Monday laying out his updated diagnosis after originally announcing he had a superficial blood clot in his left calf that caused him to miss Week 6. A follow-up scan over the weekend revealed deep vein thrombosis, and he had "bilateral pulmonary emboli," meaning several blood clots were now in his lungs.

The Eagles said Hurts' prognosis is "very good" and that he is expected to make a full recovery. However, he will be treated with blood thinners, which will take him away from football activities until he is off the treatment.

Here is the full statement:

"Over the last few days, Jalen Hurts has received comprehensive medical evaluations by physician experts. In the interest of transparency, we are providing additional information on the diagnosis and treatment plan related to his condition.

"Jalen was initially diagnosed by specialists in London with a left calf superficial vein thrombosis. After further testing and monitoring, the current diagnosis is a deep vein thrombosis, as well as bilateral pulmonary emboli. He is clinically stable and has no significant functional limitations. His treatment should only involve anticoagulation (i.e. "blood thinners"). During this time, he will not be allowed to participate in any contact activities, including football.

"Jalen's prognosis is very good, and we expect a full recovery. We anticipate that he will have the opportunity to resume contact football activities when off the blood thinners. In the meantime, he will remain active around the team and continue to condition. More importantly, we anticipate that he will have no long-term effects.

"We are thinking of Jalen and looking forward to a strong recovery."

It was initially diagnosed as a superficial blood clot. At that time, doctors advised Hurts not to sleep as a precaution, so he stayed awake for roughly 36 hours prior to the game against the Jaguars, according to reports. Despite not getting any sleep, Hurts started and threw for 220 yards and a touchdown.

Lynn has since clarified that Hurts was able to sleep despite being evaluated at the hospital until the early hours of Sunday morning. She said that the Eagles set up a room for him at the stadium.

No clots were found until Hurts was in London. It was later discovered that the blood clot was "provoked," meaning that it was caused by Hurts getting cleated in his calf during the Eagles' Week 4 loss to the Rams. That game took place a week before Philadelphia's game in London.

Hurts traveled to London that week, appearing on that week's injury report with a calf injury on Friday. He was a full practice participant that day and had no injury designation prior to the Eagles' game against the Jaguars. Hurts reportedly went to the hospital the evening prior to Sunday's game.

Philadelphia will move forward with Tanner McKee at quarterback. A 2023 sixth-round pick, McKee made his first start of the season Sunday against the Panthers. He threw for 215 yards and a touchdown in a 25-15 loss that dropped the Eagles to 2-4.

Hurts, 28, is in his seventh season with the Eagles, who selected him in the second round of the 2020 NFL Draft. During his first six seasons, Hurts earned three Pro Bowl selections and helped lead the Eagles to two NFC titles and a Super Bowl title at the end of the 2024 season. He holds the single-game Super Bowl record for rushing yards by a quarterback (72 against the Chiefs). Hurts is one of just two players (the other being Terrell Davis) to run for three touchdowns in a Super Bowl game.

Hurts was named MVP of Super Bowl LIX after amassing 293 total yards and scoring three total touchdowns in the Eagles' 40-22 win over the Chiefs. Hurts has the highest career completion percentage (73.3%) in Super Bowl history among passers with at least 40 attempts.

text:
Week 6 of the NFL season featured a star player returning from one the season’s most dramatic injuries, an important game across the pond, and another devastating loss for a Super Bowl contender.

Here’s all the action you need to know about from Sunday.

Caleb Williams picked up where he left off

Chicago Bears starting quarterback Caleb Williams played Sunday for the first time since sustaining a hamstring injury in Week 2, and he was spectacular in a 31-23 victory over the Atlanta Falcons. Williams completed 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and one touchdown, improving his completion percentage to 72.5% for the season.

Williams was especially efficient when not facing pressure. According to NFL Next Gen Stats, Williams completed all 24 of his passes from a clean pocket, the most attempts without an incompletion under such circumstances since 2018.

After going 2-1 without their starter, the Bears improved to 4-2 with the win. The offense has been humming with Williams under center, averaging 31.0 points per game in his three starts. Chicago will now enter a spotlighted stretch of its season, as the team’s next three games will all be played in primetime.

The Rams are still searching for answers

Six weeks after entering the season as a heavy favorite to win the Super Bowl, the Los Angeles Rams (2-4) are in last place in the NFC West after Sunday’s 18-16 home loss to the Arizona Cardinals.

After a frustrating day with little offense, the Rams had finally pieced together a productive drive to tie the game at 15-all in the fourth-quarter’s final minute. The point-after was no foregone conclusion. The team cut kicker Harrison Mevis after a miss in last week’s loss to Buffalo, only to see his replacement, Blake Grupe, get hurt trying to make a tackle early Sunday. That left Rams punter Ethan Evans to step up to attempt his first point-after since college — which he made to give Los Angeles a one-point lead with 47 seconds left.

It was a different kicker who ended up the hero, though. A controversial penalty on the Rams for unnecessary roughness — a penalty that increased the Cardinals’ win probability from 26% to 74% — helped Arizona’s final drive move downfield in position for Chad Ryland to attempt a game-winning kick from 43 yards. He nailed it to keep the Rams still looking for any consistency. By the way: The Rams and Chargers have one win combined inside their home stadium, SoFi Stadium, this season. The Cardinals are 2-0 there.

The Texans’ season isn’t over just yet

The Houston Texans are winners of two straight after a 34-31 victory over the Jacksonville Jaguars in London. This was the first game of the day on Sunday, and perhaps the best. Quarterbacks C.J. Stroud and Trevor Lawrence combined for 618 yards, seven touchdowns and two interceptions. Stroud was nearly perfect, posting a quarterback rating of 96.9 (out of a possible 100).

After the Texans opened up a 10-point lead in the final minute of the third quarter, the Jaguars stormed back. First, Lawrence led a nine-play, 61-yard touchdown drive to cut the score to 31-28 early in the fourth. Then, after a Travis Hunter interception, Lawrence led a 38-yard drive that culminated in a 60-yard field goal from Cam Little.

But Houston got the last laugh. After Little’s kick, the Texans quickly marched into Jacksonville territory on their ensuing possession. Ka’imi Fairbairn hit a 49-yard field goal as time expired, securing Houston’s second win of the season.

The Texans are now 2-4, and while their climb into playoff position will be an arduous one, Houston did make the postseason after an 0-3 start a year ago. If Stroud maintains his current level of play — he’s thrown nine touchdowns and only one interception so far this season — the Texans won’t be a pushover.

The Titans rose from the ranks of the winless

Tennessee’s season-long nightmare is finally over. The Titans finally won a game, knocking off their divisional rival the Indianapolis Colts 26-20. Tennessee stormed back in the second half, scoring all of its points in the final 30 minutes, including 20 in the final quarter.

The Colts aided the cause with a litany of mistakes. Quarterback Daniel Jones threw two interceptions, running back Jonathan Taylor had a fumble, the special teams had a punt blocked for a touchdown, and the offense also had a turnover on downs for good measure.

The Titans are now 1-5. Indianapolis, meanwhile, entered this season with high expectations from ownership, but fell to 2-4 after the loss.

text:
INGLEWOOD, Calif. -- Blake Grupe, the Los Angeles Rams' newest place-kicker, left Sunday's game in the first quarter because of a knee injury, and their punter, Ethan Evans, filled in by booting a go-ahead extra point in the fourth.

It didn't matter.

Evans' theatrics with 47 seconds left were short-lived as the Cardinals took the ensuing kickoff and marched downfield, winning Sunday's NFC West clash 18-16 thanks to Chad Ryland's 43-yard field goal -- his sixth of the game.

Grupe was added off the New York Jets' practice squad last week, replacing Harrison Mevis, who missed a 50-yard field goal attempt and then had a 48-yarder blocked in overtime of the Rams' loss to the Buffalo Bills last Monday.

But after making a 44-yard field goal in the opening quarter Sunday, Grupe hurt his right knee on the ensuing kickoff while trying to make a tackle, walking off the field with the assistance of the Rams' medical staff.

He was initially listed as doubtful to return but was downgraded to out in the fourth quarter.

After the game, Grupe was in the locker room with a big brace on his right leg and crutches at his locker. Coach Sean McVay said he didn't have any more details on the injury.

The Rams did not attempt another field goal in the half, but Evans was practicing place-kicking on the sideline during the game. Los Angeles did attempt a 2-point conversion after its second-quarter touchdown but did not convert. The Rams are the only team since the start of last season without a successful 2-point conversion (0-for-2), according to ESPN Research.

McVay also said the Rams ran the clock out at the end of the first half because of their kicking situation.

"Well, we're playing for a touchdown," he said. "We didn't have a field goal operation. And so the situation that we were in, that was why we approached it. If we had our normal kicker, if we had a kicker healthy, then that would've changed the approach."

Evans, though, then was thrust into action late in the fourth quarter on the shorter PAT try. Colby Parkinson's 6-yard touchdown catch tied the score at 15, and the Rams opted to kick it, with Evans converting as backup quarterback Stetson Bennett handled the snap. He said he kicked field goals in college, so he let the team know if it needed an extra point he could do it.

But Arizona marched 40 yards on five plays after that kick, with Ryland nailing a 43-yard winner as time expired for Arizona, which closed as a 13.5-point underdog and became only the second double-digit underdog to win outright in the past two seasons, per ESPN Research.

ATLANTA -- Falcons rookie linebacker Kendal Daniels was able to leave an area hospital, return to the locker room and rejoin his teammates after what appeared to be a serious-looking injury led to him getting carted off the field during Atlanta's 31-23 loss to the Chicago Bears on Sunday.

With the Bears leading 21-7 with 8:48 left in the third quarter, Daniels dived in to tackle Colston Loveland after a Caleb Williams pass completion, and the linebacker's head appeared to collide with the tight end's left leg near the knee.

Daniels remained down on the field for some time as medical personnel tended to him. They stabilized his neck and body, then loaded him onto the cart in a gurney as Falcons players and coaches gathered around and wished him well.

The team said Daniels had movement in all of his extremities and was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further evaluation. Daniels then surprisingly was able to come back to Mercedes-Benz Stadium and was walking in the locker room under his own power after the game.

On the way off the field during the third quarter, Daniels made a fist with his left hand.

"He said, 'Y'all go finish this off,'" quarterback Michael Penix Jr. said. "He was in good spirits."

Added coach Kevin Stefanski: "Those are no fun for anybody. Players, coaches. You don't want to see anyone down like that. Kendal is a kid we all love, we all respect."

Kansas City Chiefs

star tight end Travis Kelce went down with an ankle injury in the first quarter of the team's contest against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, and there is a strong chance the hit in question is going to result in a considerable punishment from the NFL.

Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley appeared to execute an illegal hip-drop tackle while bringing Kelce down, which is what resulted in the TE's ankle issue that knocked him out of the game for a brief time.

David J. Chao, a former lead team doctor in the NFL for nearly two decades, shared video of the play on social media.

Several others commented on the play in its immediate aftermath, including media members like PJ Green of The Kansas City Star.

"Daiyan Henley's tackle on Travis Kelce was a sliding hip drop where his shoulder dinged Kelce's ankle," Green wrote on X.

Chargers LB Daiyan Henley Could Face NFL Fine Upwards of $20,000

The league will review the play and its Office of Gameday Accountability will ultimately issue a ruling, though the video evidence and the widespread public sentiment is that Henley committed an illegal play on the tackle.

If the NFL agrees, the linebacker is liable to face a five-figure fine.

According to the league's official website, the initial penalty for a hip-drop tackle, which the NFL defines as an act of unnecessary roughness, is $17,911. A second offense costs the player in question a $23,822 fine.

Travis Kelce Returned to Game, Contributed to Chiefs' 5th Straight Win to Start Season

Chiefs doctors checked out Kelce multiple times on the sideline, thoroughly taping his ankle both underneath and over top of his cleat.

Kelce returned to action and had amassed 53 yards on four catches with two minutes remaining in the fourth quarter. At that junction in the contest, Kansas City held a 22-6 lead over the Chargers at Arrowhead Stadium.

text:
ATLANTA -- Caleb Williams put his right hand underneath his ear as he skipped off the field at Mercedes-Benz Stadium, a motion to encourage the raucous crowd of Chicago Bears fans on hand to get even louder.

Williams let out a guttural "Let's go!" and threw his right fist in the air following the Bears' 31-23 win over the Atlanta Falcons. The quarterback then made his way through the tunnel toward the visitors locker room where he posed a question to a handful of media members waiting to speak with him after he received one of two game balls in his return from a hamstring injury that had sidelined him the past three weeks.

"Y'all like that?" Williams said, smiling.

Williams didn't miss a beat in his return for the Bears (4-2) on Sunday, completing 30 of 36 passes for 305 yards and a touchdown and showing no physical limitations from the injury he suffered Sept. 20.

"I felt confident from the jump," Williams said of his return. "When I get out there, I'm going to feel confident in my leg, in myself and in my guys and the O-line. So I just let it rip, let these guys go make plays for us, get first downs and score touchdowns."

Williams said his body felt "great" postgame despite four sacks. With the Bears playing the New England Patriots on Thursday, Williams will prioritize treatment amid a quick turnaround.

"Felt great to get hit after three weeks of just rehabbing," he said. "So [I] feel strong, feel good. Obviously got to go and take care of it this week. It's going to be a weekly thing, just taking care of it, staying up to date on it and taking care of my body."

Chicago jumped out to a 14-0 lead in the first quarter after Williams led the offense on back-to-back touchdown drives. He completed his first 12 passes, the most at any point in a game in his career.

"Honestly, I didn't even know that he hadn't missed yet," coach Ben Johnson said. "That's not even something -- it's more you just kind of calling it. You're doing what you feel like is going to help your guys out. But when I reflect back, it's not a surprise. I know we had a couple big plays there on third-and-long that were really the key part of keeping those drives going there early in the game.

"The fact that we started fast, really in all three phases, was huge for us, as well as something that we had also talked about the night before. Just if you could write a script, that's what we would want to do against a team like this. We've got to come out of the gate hot, and it's a dangerous team. Their defense is darn good. Their offense can put up points in a hurry, as we saw at the end of the game. And I thought the way that our guys came out and responded was huge. Having Caleb back was a huge part of it."

The Bears went 9-of-17 on third down, which allowed the offense to extend drives and stay on the field for 40:08. After entering Week 6 with the league's worst red zone scoring efficiency (42.86%), the Bears were 4-for-4 Sunday, excluding Williams' kneel-down at the end of the game.

Ahead of the Bears' trip to Atlanta, Williams completed his first week of practice with full participation since suffering what he classified as a "pretty serious" hamstring tear late in a Week 2 loss to the Minnesota Vikings.

Midway through the week, Williams had a one-on-one meeting with Johnson in which he voiced a desire to open up the passing attack upon his return.

"I walked in his office, dapped him up and said, 'Let's get this thing going this week,'" Williams said. "I walked out after that."

That approach paid off quickly Sunday.

"He was connecting everywhere," wide receiver Rome Odunze said. "People were making plays all over the field. So our offense was really clicking. That's why we want to be in that flow state mode, and we were in there today."

In the process of recording his sixth career 300-yard passing game, which broke a tie with Mitchell Trubisky for the most such games by a Bears player before turning 25 years old, Williams set a career-high completion percentage (83%). He also completed all 26 of his attempts when Atlanta failed to generate pressure, which marked the most attempts without an incompletion since ESPN began tracking pressures in 2009.

Days after Williams expressed frustration over how his hamstring injury was reported and the negative reaction he received on social media for his emotions after getting injured, his teammates rallied in support of the quarterback and the energy his return provided.

title: Rams kicker Blake Grupe doubtful to return with knee injury after attempting tackle on kickoff return
description:
The Los Angeles Rams' special teams woes continued with a very odd situation Sunday, with kicker Blake Grupe being ruled out of the game with a knee injury after attempting a tackle.
That left punter Ethan Evans as the only option for the Rams at kicker, with the 25-year-old attempting — and making — his first extra point in his NFL career.
With no other kicker on the roster, Evans filled in if the Rams need to attempt a field goal or extra point.

text:
The Los Angeles Rams' special teams woes continued with a very odd situation Sunday, with kicker Blake Grupe being ruled out of the game with a knee injury after attempting a tackle. That left punter Ethan Evans as the only option for the Rams at kicker, with the 25-year-old attempting — and making — his first extra point in his NFL career.

Just days after he signed with the team as a free agent, Grupe started against the Arizona Cardinals in Week 6, scoring a field goal in the first quarter. But on the kickoff, Grupe broke up a 40-yard return from Devin Duvernay by knocking the Cardinals receiver out of bounds — and Grupe paid for it.

Grupe went into the locker room before he was eventually ruled doubtful. He was later downgraded to out.

With no other kicker on the roster, Evans filled in if the Rams need to attempt a field goal or extra point.

With the shaky kicker situation, the Rams tried to avoid kicking when possible. After scoring a touchdown in the second quarter, the team went for a 2-point conversion. Matthew Stafford was sacked and fumbled on the attempt, with the Cardinals recovering.

Other plays indicated a reluctance to use Evans. Late in the first half, the Rams got the ball at their own 35-yard-line with 46 seconds remaining, but opted to let the clock run out instead of get closer to the end zone. In the fourth quarter, Los Angeles went for it on fouth-and-8 at the Arizona 44, out of field-goal range; the Rams failed to convert.

As the Rams tied things up with a touchdown with a minute remaining, they had to rely on Evans for the go-ahead extra point. Evans, who had placekicking duties in college and high school, had never attempted an extra point in the NFL — but he nailed it.

The Cardinals, however, beat the Rams 18-16 after hitting a walk-off field goal. The loss puts Los Angeles at a stunning 2-4 record.

Grupe was signed by the Rams earlier last week as a free agent, replacing Harrison Mevis as the starting kicker. Los Angeles waived Mevis after he missed two field goals (one was blocked) in last week's three-point loss to the Buffalo Bills.

Evans has spent his entire NFL career with the Rams, getting selected in the seventh round of the 2023 NFL Draft.

What happened to Mike McCarthy?

text:
Pittsburgh Steelers coach Mike McCarthy coached the second half of his team's NFL Week 6 game against Tampa Bay with a foot injury.

The 62-year-old told reporters after his team's 26-19 victory that his foot was stepped on leading up to halftime. The CBS broadcast reported that the 62-year-old spent halftime in the blue medical tent on the Steelers' sideline instead of joining his team in the locker room. He was seen limping on the field at Raymond James Stadium, favoring his right foot.

"Mike McCarthy, heading off the field, and appears to have twisted his ankle," CBS play-by-play announcer Andrew Catalon observed as the broadcast returned from studio coverage at the half. "You can see him slow up, and then needing a little assistance.

"He went right into the blue medical tent, and he spent the entire halftime in the tent. He just came out. He never went to the locker room at halftime as he was getting his leg looked at."

What happened to Mike McCarthy?

CBS sideline reporter AJ Ross called the injury a "freak thing" as McCarthy was walking to speak with her at halftime. Cameras did not capture exactly what happened, but he told reporters that the discomfort was caused by being stepped on and not by rolling his ankle.

The veteran is in his first season as coach of his hometown team after 18 seasons with Green Bay and Dallas. He is the offense's play-caller, so any departure from the playing surface would have been a change to the team's process.

Quarterback Aaron Rodgers said afterward that the injury disrupted little about the team's routine, though there was concern among players.

"There wasn't a whole lot different at halftime," Rodgers said. "It was still the same chaos, but people said Mike didn't come in and people were wondering what the heck's going on. Is he OK? Glad he's OK."

Cameras showed McCarthy standing on the sideline throughout the second half, so the mishap did not appear to impact his ability to stay involved in the game. His offense rallied from a 13-3 halftime deficit to tie the game late in the fourth quarter, then win in overtime.

title: Kendal Daniels Injury Announcement Includes Details On Hospital, If He's Moving
description:
Kendal Daniels was carted off the field on Sunday on a back board.
The Atlanta Falcons' rookie linebacker was injured on a tackle attempt, and it was a scary moment.
Kendal Daniels Hospital Update The Falcons shared on social media that Daniels was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further evaluation.
Is Kendal Daniels Moving?
Who is Kendal Daniels?
text:
Kendal Daniels was carted off the field on Sunday on a back board.

The Atlanta Falcons' rookie linebacker was injured on a tackle attempt, and it was a scary moment. He had his teammates surrounding him on the field, many looking distraught.

Once Daniels was carted away, fans and players and coaches were all waiting to hear whether he was doing OK.

Less than an hour later, an announcement was made to provide more details on what had happened.

Kendal Daniels Hospital Update

The Falcons shared on social media that Daniels was taken to Grady Memorial Hospital for further evaluation.

That's the public hospital for the city of Atlanta.

It's the 10th-largest public hospital in the United States and is a Level I trauma center.

Is Kendal Daniels Moving?

The Falcons update did share that Daniels was able to move all his extremeties.

Given the fact that he laid immobile on the turf, that's a crucial update.

Who is Kendal Daniels?

Daniels is a rookie linebacker and 23 years old. He's originally from the state of Oklahoma, where he was ranked No. 5 among the safety class in his senior year of high school.

He split his college career between Oklahoma State and Oklahoma. He was the Big 12 Defensive Freshman of the Year at OSU.

He's an impressive athlete, measuring 6-foot-5 and 242 pounds. He ran a 4.76-second 40-yard dash at the NFL Combine and vertical leaped 29.5 inches.

Daniels was chosen by the Falcons in the fourth round of the 2026 NFL Draft at the No. 134 overall pick.

Entering Sunday, he had played in five games in his rookie season. He had 22 tackles, including 2.0 tackles for loss. He has 1.0 sack and one pass defensed so far this season.

Daniels was having the best game of his career on Sunday. He already had seven tackles, including one for a loss.

His playing time had increased because Divine Deablo had already exited the game with an arm injury and been ruled out.

What Happened to Kendal Daniels?

Daniels attempted a low tackle on Chicago Bears tight end Colston Loveland.

Loveland's right knee hit Daniels directly in the facemask, though, essentially a smash right to the front of his head.

It left Daniels on the ground for quick attention from the trainers, and at least the first update from the Falcons is a good one relative to how the scene on the field looked.

text:
The Los Angeles Rams' kicking conundrum continues into Week 6, but not in the way you'd expect. After cutting former placekicker Harrison Mevis after Week 5, L.A. seemingly found its solution after signing veteran Blake Grupe to assume the kicking duties. The former Notre Dame kicker made his Rams debut on Sunday and quickly endeared himself to his new squad by netting a 44-yard field goal in the first quarter.

However, things went downhill after that. Grupe is now doubtful to return to Sunday's contest due to a knee injury, the team announced. Grupe suffered the injury while making a tackle on the kickoff following his made field goal. He was seen lowering his shoulder to hit returner Devin Duvernay and came down awkwardly.

With Grupe sidelined, the entire kicking operation is reshuffled. Punter Ethan Evans will serve as the kicker, while receiver Jordan Whittington could be the holder, as ESPN notes he was working on holds along the sideline.

After that, he made stops with the Colts and Jets before finding his way to the Rams. title: Patriots' Romeo Doubs hurt on 42-yard TD catch vs. Jets - ESPN
authors: Mike Reiss, Ben Solak, ESPN Fantasy, Mel Kiper Jr, Jordan Reid, Cameron Wolfe, Michael DiRocco, Brooke Pryor, Brianna Williams, NFL Nation
description:
-- On the day the New England Patriots welcomed back receiver A.J.
Brown, they lost their other top receiver, Romeo Doubs, to a shoulder injury.
Doubs left Sunday's 26-19 win over the New York Jets after diving to haul in a 42-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Drake Maye with 4:10 remaining in the first quarter.
In addition to Doubs, Patriots starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker injured his hamstring in the second quarter and was later ruled out.
Starting right tackle Morgan Moses also left the game in the second quarter due to an ankle injury.
text:
FOXBOROUGH, Mass. -- On the day the New England Patriots welcomed back receiver A.J. Brown, they lost their other top receiver, Romeo Doubs, to a shoulder injury.

Doubs left Sunday's 26-19 win over the New York Jets after diving to haul in a 42-yard touchdown pass from quarterback Drake Maye with 4:10 remaining in the first quarter. He was initially announced as questionable to return before the team ruled him out early in the third quarter.

Doubs landed hard on his shoulder on the play after reaching a top speed of 21.44 mph to track down Maye's heave, according to NFL Next Gen Stats, which was the fastest speed he has reached as the ball carrier in his five-year career. The Patriots signed him to a four-year, $68 million deal in March as one of their top free agent targets, then traded for Brown in June to give Maye a new 1-2 combination.

Brown hurt his ankle in Week 1, was placed on injured reserve and returned to game action Sunday.

In addition to Doubs, Patriots starting left guard Alijah Vera-Tucker injured his hamstring in the second quarter and was later ruled out.

Starting right tackle Morgan Moses also left the game in the second quarter due to an ankle injury. After initially being announced as questionable to return, he was downgraded to out at the start of the fourth quarter.

And guard/center Ben Brown was ruled out in the fourth quarter with a knee injury.

The Patriots (4-2) have a quick turnaround after Sunday's game, visiting the Chicago Bears on Thursday.

Coach Mike Vrabel said he didn't have definitive updates on any of the players, but cast doubt that they would be available for that game.

"We are all smart people here; it's a short week," Vrabel said. "Whether they can make it back or not, I don't know. They didn't finish [this] game and that's a quick turnaround."

title: Will Kyle Monangai Return in Week 7? Injury and Timeline Updates for Chicago Bears RB
description:

text:
The Chicago Bears once again didn't have the services of running back Kyle Monangai for the Week 6 game against the Atlanta Falcons.

Monangai suffered a turf toe injury in Week 4 against the New York Jets and that kept him from playing in Week 5 versus the Green Bay Packers.

There was no progress for Monangai in Week 6, at least in terms of his practice participation, as the former seventh-round pick did not practice at all before being ruled out.

After two absences in a row for Monangai, here's what we know about his return timeline moving forward.

Kyle Monangai's return timeline

As head coach Ben Johnson said again this past week, there is no plan to put Monangai on injured reserve, which would have forced him to sit out a minimum of four games.

That means the Bears don't expect Monangai to sit out more than three games, which on the surface puts him in play to return in Week 7 against the New England Patriots.

However, the Bears have to play on a short week, with the game versus the Patriots taking place on Thursday, so Monangai won't have as much time as he normally would to get right, and it looks like he's going to need every day he can get since he still hasn't practiced since his injury.

Knowing all that, it's safe to assume that Monangai is going to be back in Week 8 against the Seattle Seahawks, at the earliest, instead of Week 7.

With the short week, the Bears will release their first injury report on Monday, and that injury report will likely be an estimation.

That said, any semblance of estimated participation would be good news for Monangai's chances of suiting up.

Kyle Monangai injury update

Last week, head coach Ben Johnson provided a positive update on Monangai.

While Johnson said once again that Monanga is week-to-week, he also noted how the Bears running back should avoid injured reserve and he's progressing in his recovery.

"It wasn't something we felt required an IR stint. It remains a week-to-week situation, but as far as I know, he's continuing to trend in the right direction," Johnson told reporters.

While it remains to be seen if Monangai will be back for Week 7 — again, we're skeptical that will happen — Johnson's update shows Monangai is getting better and that leaves us optimistic he won't be out longer than Week 8.

The Bears could certainly use their second-year back, as Chicago does not have another player like him on the roster and the offense just isn't the same without the Monangai-Swift duo.

text:
Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy wasn't able to address his team as usual at halftime on Sunday in their overtime win against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers.

On his way to his halftime interview at Raymond James Stadium, McCarthy apparently injured his ankle.

Broadcast cameras did not appear to catch the injury on video. Instead, McCarthy was shown having trouble as he tried to walk off the field at halftime. He eventually decided to head straight into the blue medical tent on the sideline, where he remained for all of halftime. He never made it back to the locker room to address the Steelers, and re-joined the team at the start of the third quarter.

Despite the injury, McCarthy continued coaching the team in the second half normally. His ankle injury appeared to be minor after all.

And, despite falling into a 13-point hole in the fourth quarter, Aaron Rodgers led the Steelers storming back to force overtime. He eventually found Germie Bernard for a 6-yard touchdown pass in the extra period, too. The score was the first of Bernard's career, and lifted the Steelers to a second straight win.

Rodgers went 33-of-49 passing for 253 yards with two touchdowns and an interception in the win, which moved the Steelers to 4-2 on the season. They are in a great spot in the AFC North race, but the win in Tampa was much more complicated than it needed to be. Rodgers could have sealed the win in regulation, but couldn't find the end zone from the 3-yard line after Buccaneers quarterback Jalon Daniels threw his second interception of the fourth quarter.

But a win is a win, and McCarthy's halftime injury didn't appear to hinder him much in the end. He and the Steelers can head home happy.

OCTOBER 18: The news on Henderson is better than expected. Ian Rapoport of the NFL Network reports the second-year RB is expected to play against the Jets in Week 6. Ditto left tackle Will Campbell, whose MCL sprain was expected to force him to miss time. With Brown also set to return, the Pats are getting closer to full strength.

OCTOBER 17: The Patriots are getting wide receiver A.J. Brown back from injured reserve in Week 6, but another of their notable offensive weapons could miss time. Running back TreVeyon Henderson has a high ankle sprain that is expected to shelve him for multiple games, according to Adam Schefter of ESPN.

Henderson will not require surgery, per Schefter, and an IR stint may not be necessary in this case. Although Henderson confirmed the sprain to Mike Reiss of ESPN and other reporters on Friday, he managed to practice on a limited basis this week.

The Patriots list Henderson as questionable on their injury report, leaving open the possibility that he could play against the AFC East rival Jets on Sunday. If Henderson can’t go, the Patriots will elevate Lan Larison from the practice squad to join Rhamondre Stevenson and Corey Kiner as their backfield options, Reiss relays.

While splitting time with Stevenson in 2025, Henderson impressed during a 17-game rookie season. The second-round pick from Ohio State ran for 911 yards on 180 carries (good for a robust 5.1 average per attempt) and scored nine touchdowns. He also found the end zone once as a pass catcher and finished with 35 receptions for 221 yards on 42 targets. This season has not gone as smoothly for Henderson, who missed a Week 1 loss to the Seahawks with a different ankle injury and has rushed for just 163 yards on 42 attempts (3.9 YPC) in four games. He also hasn’t been as big of a factor through the air, having caught two of four targets for 22 yards.

On the other side of the ball, the 3-2 Patriots have had to make do without starting edge defender Harold Landry all season. Landry led the team in sacks (8.5) during its AFC title-winning campaign in 2025, but he began battling knee problems midway through the year. Those issues have continued into 2026, which forced the Patriots to place Landry on reserve/PUP at the end of August. While they still haven’t opened Landry’s 21-day practice window, head coach Mike Vrabel said Friday that “the plan would be for him to return at some point” (via Andrew Callahan of the Boston Herald).

text:
Jalen Hurts will be sidelined for at least a month as he undergoes treatment for a superficial blood clot in his calf.

The Philadelphia Eagles placed their star quarterback on injured reserve Saturday afternoon, the team announced.

Hurts is set to miss at least the next four games, and on Sunday against the Carolina Panthers will be replaced by QB Tanner McKee as the Eagles' starting quarterback.

NFL Network Insider Ian Rapoport and ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that Philadelphia's decision to place Hurts on IR came after consultations with numerous doctors and experts about how to treat the signal-caller's blood clot.

The team first announced Hurts was dealing with a blood clot when they declared him out for Sunday's contest, and while doing so released a statement regarding the injury timeline.

Hurts sought medical treatment for his calf on Oct. 8 after he was cleated during Philadelphia's Week 4 loss to the Los Angeles Rams, according to the statement. On Oct. 10, team medical staff performed an ultrasound following the Eagles' flight to London and a walkthrough session ahead of their Week 5 game against the Jacksonville Jaguars. The ultrasound revealed the blood clot, but doctors determined it was safe for Hurts to play.

He went 21 of 40 for 220 yards and a touchdown in another losing effort, but practiced back in the United States on Wednesday before undergoing a follow-up ultrasound that revealed movement in the blood clot.

The indication of movement set in motion the events this week, with the Eagles initially ruling Hurts out and gathering myriad medical opinions before opting to place him on IR.

Hurts heads to the sideline having lost three straight games to fall to 2-3. He's thrown for 933 yards, eight touchdowns and three interceptions this season with a 57.8 completion percentage that stands as a career low outside his rookie season.

His struggles are emblematic of an Eagles squad that has been in disarray due to injuries, performance and seemingly everything in between.

Wide receiver DeVonta Smith and tight end Dallas Goedert will be at McKee's disposal against Carolina, but they have each missed two games. Running back Saquon Barkley is set to miss his second contest due to a hamstring injury, and his primary backups, Tank Bigsby and Will Shipley, are on IR, leaving the Eagles to turn to Dameon Pierce and Carson Steele in the backfield. Right tackle Lane Johnson abruptly retired on Oct. 6 after 13-plus seasons and six Pro Bowls, and Cam Jurgens, a Pro Bowler the past two seasons who endured a dreadful start to the '26 campaign, was traded to the Houston Texans a day later.

It's culminated in an offense that ranks 29th in points scored, which would match the franchise's worst finish since 2012. The Eagles haven't finished a season 30th in yards -- where they currently sit -- since 1999.

The onus to turn it around now shifts to McKee, who has thrown for 597 yards, five TDs and one INT in six career appearances with a 1-1 record as a starter. Behind him is Joe Milton III, signed off the Dallas Cowboys' practice squad on Friday, and fifth-round rookie Cole Payton.

It's time for Nick Sirianni's crew to dig deep if they're to run the coach's streak of playoff berths to six since he took over the job.

In the meantime, Hurts will get the treatment he needs to ensure he returns to full health.

text:
Micah Parsons won't be on the field for a highly anticipated prime-time grudge match when his Green Bay Packers host the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday, Oct. 18.

When might the three-time All-Pro edge rusher actually come make his comeback?

Ten months after he suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament and meniscus in his left knee, Parsons remains on the physically unable to perform list.

Yet while others were eager to see him square off against his former team with the "Sunday Night Football" spotlight firmly trained on him, the pass rusher said he wasn't going to expedite his recovery process just to make it back in time for the matchup.

"So many people wanted me to be back for that game to make the game bigger than what it was," Parsons said last week on his podcast, "The Edge with Micah Parsons." "It's just another 'Sunday Night Football' game between two good teams. It's not about me. I think that probably let people down. 'Oh, Micah, he's gonna want to be back for the Dallas game.' No, I'm in that phase of life where I just want to be healthy again. That's it."

Micah Parsons injury update

Parsons has yet to be cleared to practice. Now set to sit out the Week 6 contest, the edge rusher will miss out on what he said over the summer would be the "most optimistic" timetable for a return.

In Parsons' mind, however, the wait for his season debut could end soon.

"If the Super Bowl was this week, I'm playing in the Super Bowl," Parsons said on his podcast. "But it's just about me making sure I have all the small things fixed first.

"What a lot of people don't figure out is it's not just the ACL. It's like, why did the ACL (tear) happen? What was weak? Because it all works together. It's a chain. And throughout the history of ACL, they notice if you come back early, there tends to be an overcompensation injury on the other side."

Packers coach Matt LaFleur, who last week said he would play Parsons as soon as he was given "the green light," echoed that sentiment.

"(S)ometimes, you’ve got to make sure that your body is (in sync)," LaFleur said. "You don’t want one leg to be that much stronger than the other leg is what I’m getting at.”

The Packers don't have their bye until Week 11, with a difficult stretch looming before the break. After the clash with the Cowboys, Green Bay faces the Detroit Lions on the road before hosting a "Thursday Night Football" showdown with the NFC South-leading Carolina Panthers. A trip to take on the New England Patriots and a home game against the undefeated Minnesota Vikings then follow before the break.

How Packers defense is faring without Micah Parsons

Pressing on without Parsons has not been without its challenges for the Packers, who wilted down the stretch last season after their star defensive player was lost for the season in December.

Green Bay's most dramatic display on defense came in a Week 3 unraveling against the Atlanta Falcons on "Thursday Night Football." With quarterback Michael Penix Jr. returning to the lineup, Atlanta's previously dormant attack exploded for 498 yards in a 35-14 win. Running back Bijan Robinson rolled to 194 yards on the ground, while wide receiver Drake London added another 194 yards through the air.

From there, however, the Packers seemed to settle in with consecutive victories over the Tampa Bay Buccaneers and Chicago Bears, allowing a combined 21 points in the two contests.

Green Bay's pass rush has managed to generate a good deal of heat on opposing quarterbacks without Parsons in the fold, ranking fifth in pressure rate (42.5%), according to Next Gen Stats. Former first-round pick Lukas Van Ness, who largely struggled throughout his first three years as a pro, has stepped up to help fill the void by recording 21 pressures, the 10th-highest sum of any defender in the NFL so far this year.

But with all of their wins coming against offenses that have either been muted or shorthanded – the Bears were without quarterback Caleb Williams and running back Kyle Monangai in their loss – the Packers figure to be in for a sizable test in the coming weeks. Their next three opponents rank in the top eight for both scoring and EPA per play. The defense will also be without one of its other stars for the rest of the season after linebacker Edgerrin Cooper suffered a season-ending torn Achilles in Week 4.
